title: Grateful Dead Live at Fox Theatre on 1971-03-18
lineage: SBD > (7inch) MR > Cass > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard captures a high‑energy 1971 Fox show highlighted by a stellar Caution and powerful Other One, despite occasional tape cuts.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers a clear soundboard mix that showcases the band’s fiery spring‑71 performance at the Fox Theatre. Highlights include an incendiary Caution, a soaring Other One suite and tight renditions of Wharf Rat, Not Fade Away and Bertha, while a few first‑set cuts and occasional hiss remind listeners it’s an early‑70s tape. Overall the show is praised for its energy and Pigpen’s organ/vocal contributions, making it a must‑listen for fans of this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers award 4–5 stars and emphasize strong musical performance with only minor recording flaws; the weighted average of show (≈70%) and recording (≈30%) yields a rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean, well‑balanced soundboard tape with occasional hiss, tape‑flip/cut sections (Other One, Truckin', Casey Jones) and a few level issues (Jerry’s guitar low in the mix). Overall very listenable.

standout_songs: The Other One > Jam > Caution suite
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two solid two‑hour sets; the first set is strong but a bit uneven, while the second set builds momentum with a blazing Other One suite leading into the iconic Caution. Transitions are generally tight despite the occasional missing segment.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals praised as “excellent” and “slicing”; guitar tone noted as good though occasionally low in the mix, experimental on some jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s runs described as “overdrive,” vocal contributions highlighted; his rhythm work praised especially on NFA > GDTRFB.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ and pedal‑steel work on Wharf Rat and other numbers singled out as a major highlight; keyboards generally noted as solid.
band_member_comments.Drums: Percussion solo remembered as lengthy and impressive; overall drum work considered solid though not heavily commented.
